questions.question: Which part of the computer actually follows a program's instructions?
questions.explanation: The CPU is the 'chef': it fetches, decodes and executes instructions. RAM and storage only hold data.

questions.question: What happens to the contents of RAM when the computer turns off?
questions.explanation: RAM is fast, short-term memory that needs power. That's why you save files to storage (the SSD), which keeps data without power.

questions.question: When you run `python3 hello.py`, what does the Python interpreter do?
options: It translates your Python code into steps the CPU can perform
It sends your code to Python's website to run
It turns your code into a picture
It deletes the file after running it
questions.explanation: The CPU only understands machine code. The interpreter reads your Python and carries it out step by step on the CPU.

questions.question: What's the job of the operating system (like macOS)?
options: Only to show the desktop wallpaper
To manage the hardware and all the other running programs
questions.explanation: The OS decides which program uses the CPU, keeps programs' memory separate, and handles files, the screen and the network for them.
